'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[London, Ontario truck attack]]
**Four people are killed and another is injured after a man drives his truck into a [[Pakistanis in Canada|Pakistani]] [[Islam in Canada|Muslim]] family in [[London, Ontario]], [[Canada]]. The suspect is identified by police as Nathaniel Veltman, a local 20-year-old motivated by [[Islamophobia]]. He has been arrested and facing four charges of [[first-degree murder]] and one charge of [[attempted murder]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/7/canada-family-targeted-in-fatal-anti-muslim-attack-police-say (Al Jazeera English)] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/london/london-pedestrians-killed-man-in-custody-1.6056238 (CBC News)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***A truck carrying explosives is detonated at the police headquarters in [[Balkh Province|Balkh]], killing 16 people and injuring 117 others. In addition to the district building that was completely destroyed and the police headquarters that was nearly demolished, 10 houses and 80 shops were also damaged in the attack. The Taliban claimed responsibility for the attack. [https://tolonews.com/afghanistan-172725 (TOLO)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[British Normandy Memorial]] in [[Normandy]], [[France]], is officially unveiled on the 77th anniversary of the [[Normandy landings]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-57373932 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Bangladesh]]
*****[[Bangladesh]] approves the emergency use of the [[Sinovac]] [[CoronaVac]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]], becoming the second Chinese-made vaccine to be approved in the country. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/06/06/sinovac-covid-19-vaccine-approved-for-emergency-use (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Haryana]]
*****[[Dera Sacha Sauda]] chief [[Gurmeet Ram Rahim Singh]], who is currently serving prison time in [[Rohtak]], tests positive for [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.indiatvnews.com/news/india/gurmeet-ram-rahim-singh-tests-positive-for-covid19-709785 (India TV)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Israel]]
*****[[Israel]] begins a vaccination campaign for 600,000 children between the ages of 12 and 16, with the first priority being children who are at greater risk of experiencing severe symptoms from COVID-19 and children from families who are expected to travel abroad. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/starting-sunday-600000-israeli-teens-eligible-for-covid-19-vaccine/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
*****The [[United States]] surpasses 300 million doses of [[COVID-19 vaccine]]s being administered. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/us-surpasses-300-million-covid-19-vaccine-shots/story?id=78119122 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Yukon]]
*****An outbreak is declared at a [[gold mine]] in [[Yukon]] after three people tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/north/outbreak-yukon-gold-mine-1.6055374 (CBC News)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
***[[Fiji]] reports a record 83 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the national total of confirmed cases to 604. The [[Ministry of Health (Fiji)|Ministry of Health]] seals off the [[Colonial War Memorial Hospital]] in [[Suva]] for COVID-19 patients only as 11 of the cases are of unconfirmed origin. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/444172/fiji-records-83-covid-cases-its-highest-daily-total-yet (RNZ International)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**Israeli police arrest [[Sheikh Jarrah]] activists Muna and [[Mohammed El-Kurd]], the former for allegedly participating in riots, and the latter after he turned himself in following a police summons. Both of them were released separately. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-middle-east-57376550 (BBC News)]
*[[Aftermath of the 2021 United States Capitol attack]]
**[[United States House of Representatives|U.S. Rep.]] [[Eric Swalwell]] ([[Democratic Party (United States)|D]]-[[California|CA]]) announces he has served [[Mo Brooks]] ([[Republican Party (United States)|R]]-[[Alabama|AL]]) with a lawsuit that accuses him of being responsible for inciting the [[2021 United States Capitol attack|January 6 riot]] at the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.axios.com/eric-swalwell-mo-brooks-lawsuit-served-capitol-riot-b41dc3e6-f00f-44ed-87c7-89e4cecc3c66.html (''Axios'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Saxony-Anhalt state election]]
**Voters in the [[States of Germany|German State]] of [[Saxony-Anhalt]] head to the polls to elect a new [[Landtag of Saxony-Anhalt|Landtag]]. They are the last German elections before the [[2021 German federal election]]. [https://www.saltwire.com/nova-scotia/news/east-german-state-votes-in-final-test-before-national-election-100596640/ (SaltWire Network)]
**In a surprise victory, [[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]]'s party [[Christian Democratic Union of Germany|Christian Democratic Union]] (CDU) is projected to be the clear winner, taking in 37% of the vote. The far-right [[Alternative for Germany]], which was polling neck-and-neck with the CDU for most of the campaign, came in second with 20.8%, down three percentage points from [[2016 Saxony-Anhalt state election|last state election]]. [https://www.dw.com/en/germanys-cdu-gets-boost-with-surprise-victory/a-57795626 (Deutsche Welle)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/east-german-state-votes-final-test-before-election-decide-who-replaces-merkel-2021-06-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Peruvian general election]]
**[[Peruvians]] head to the polls to elect their [[President of Peru|President]]. [[Left-wing]] candidate [[Pedro Castillo]] faces [[right-wing]] candidate [[Keiko Fujimori]], who is the daughter of the authoritarian former President [[Alberto Fujimori]]. Polls show Fujimori slightly ahead in the polls as Castillo warns of fraud. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/peruvians-head-polls-elect-president-divided-by-class-geography-2021-06-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[2021 Somaliland parliamentary election]]
**The National Electoral Council reports that in [[Somaliland]]'s  first parliamentary election since [[2005 Somaliland parliamentary election|2005]], oppositional parties [[Waddani]] and [[Justice and Welfare Party]] won 31 and 21 seats respectively, while the ruling [[Kulmiye Peace, Unity, and Development Party]] won 30 seats. The victorious oppositional parties subsequently announce that they will form a government together. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/6/somaliland-opposition-wins-first-parliamentary-polls-since (Al Jazeera English)]
*[[2021 Mexican legislative election]]
**[[Mexico|Mexican]] voters head to the polls to elect [[LXV Legislature of the Mexican Congress|a new session]] to the [[Chamber of Deputies (Mexico)|Chamber of Deputies]]. Analysts predict that while [[President of Mexico|President]] [[Andrés Manuel López Obrador]]'s party [[National Regeneration Movement]] will lose seats, [[Juntos Hacemos Historia|his coalition]] will retain an overall majority. The lead-up to the election saw considerable violence, with at least 89 politicians, including 35 candidates, killed in the past 200 days. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/6/polls-open-in-mexicos-widely-anticipated-midterm-elections (Al Jazeera English)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 U.S. Women's Open]]
**In [[golf]], 19-year-old [[Yuka Saso]] of the [[Philippines]] wins this year's [[U.S. Women's Open|championship]] at the [[Olympic Club]] in [[San Francisco]], [[California]], after [[Comeback (sports)|coming back]] from two [[Par (score)|double-bogeys]] to beat [[Japan]]'s [[Nasa Hataoka]] in the third hole of a [[Playoff (golf)#Sudden death|sudden death playoff]]. Saso is the first Filipino player to win a major golf championship and equals [[South Korea]]'s [[Inbee Park]] as the youngest champion of the U.S. Women's Open. [https://edition.cnn.com/2021/06/06/golf/yuka-saso-us-womens-open-golf-spt-intl-hnk/index.html (CNN International)]
*[[2019–20 CONCACAF Nations League]]
**The [[United States men's national soccer team|United States]] wins the inaugural edition of the [[CONCACAF Nations League]], defeating [[Mexico national football team|Mexico]] in [[2021 CONCACAF Nations League Final|the final]] by a scoreline of 3–2 after extra time. [https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=570981 (ESPN)]
